surfaces.part: ridge band at top of roof (back brown strip)

answer.evidence: The main body is a house with a large thatched roof plane (rows 19-40, about 22 rows) that widens from 76 to 88 px, with a dark eave line and shadow at rows 41-43 above the front wall. The roof is a sloped plane, evidence (c). The front wall (rows 44-85) has plaster, a door, windows and a veranda, giving about 41 rows of front face. The veranda at rows 76-83 shows a lighter top edge, which also reads as a horizontal surface. No isometric side face is drawn. Overall it reads as three-quarter.

styleAnswer.evidence: The measured facts put the candidate at or above both references on density: 13 visible tones per tile against 12 and 10. Near-flat coverage is 3%, which is negligible and close to the references' 0%. By eye, the thatch roof carries streaked grain and moss-like clumps in about 4-5 lightness steps, which is slightly fewer than the roof tiles on the references. The plaster wall, the shoji lattice, the wooden posts and the stone footings each have their own tone variation, so there are no large flat fills. Outlines mostly lean dark olive or brown next to the thatch and wood, but 33% of the dark edge pixels are near-neutral, against 7-9% on the references. That is why I call the outline mixed rather than fully material-toned. It is not a uniform black sticker line, since forms are often separated by value alone. The piece is not shallow overall, and a careful artist would accept it next to the references.

surfaces.part: thatched roof slope (ridge cap rows 20-23 plus thatch rows 24-40)

answer.evidence: The main body is a farmhouse with a large sloped thatched roof plane in rows 20-40. The column scan shows a ridge band at rows 20-23 and thatch texture at rows 24-40. A dark front-edge line at row 41 and eave shadow at rows 41-42 end the roof, and the wall face of about 42 rows (44-85) sits below it. The roof is far wider than the wall, with widths growing from 76 to 90 px down the slope. The veranda in front also shows a lighter top plank band at rows 76-80 and a darker front face below. There is no receding side face, so the view is south-facing 3/4.

styleAnswer.evidence: The measured facts are at or above the references: 13 visible tones per tile against 12 and 10, 3% near-flat coverage against 0%, and 33% neutral dark edges against 7% and 9%. By eye, the thatch roof has streaked grain, moss-green patches and a darker eave band, about 4-5 steps.
